'''Derrick Bernard Favors'''<ref>{{cite web|title=Derrick Favors|url=https://www.nba.com/players/derrick/favors/202324|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 2, 2018}}</ref> (born July 15, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA G League]]. Favors played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]] for one season before being selected by the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]] with the third overall pick of the [[2010 NBA draft]].

After playing a season with the Nets, Favors was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in 2011, where he played for eight seasons. In the 2019 offseason, he was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He then returned to the Jazz in the 2020–2021 season after playing a year with the Pelicans.

During his second stint with the Utah Jazz, Favors became the franchise's 10th all-time leading scorer when he passed [[Mehmet Okur]].

==High school career==
Favors played [[basketball#High school basketball|high school basketball]] at [[South Atlanta High School]], where he was ranked as one of the best high school basketball players in the class of 2009. [[Scout.com]] rated him the #1 player in the country,<ref>[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2009 Favors #1 by Scout]. Scouthoops.scout.com. Retrieved on June 14, 2011.</ref> #2 in the [[ESPNU]]100,<ref>[http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100 Favors #2 by ESPNU] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100826023439/http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100 |date=August 26, 2010 }}. Insider.espn.go.com. Retrieved on June 14, 2011.</ref> and #4 by [[Rivals.com]]. On March 14, 2009, he led South Atlanta to the Georgia Class AAA state championship. He scored 38 points and had 21 rebounds in the championship game against [[Westover Comprehensive High School|Westover High School]].<ref>[http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player?page=onthetrail&recruitId=43657&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fplayer%3fpage%3donthetrail%26recruitId%3d43657 Derrick Favors caps career in style] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090604020913/http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player?page=onthetrail&recruitId=43657&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fplayer%3fpage%3donthetrail%26recruitId%3d43657 |date=June 4, 2009 }}. Insider.espn.go.com. Retrieved on June 14, 2011.</ref> He was named to the 2009 [[McDonald's All-American Team]]. He led the East to a 113–110 victory and was named the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the game. He scored 19 points and had 8 rebounds.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4035376 Favors Named MVP of McDonalds All American Game].</ref> Favors was selected to participate in the 2009 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Portland, Oregon]] but pulled out for personal reasons<ref>[http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Nike-Hoop-Summit-International-Rosters-Announced-3145/ Derrick Favors Pulls Out of Nike Hoop Summit] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201204120825/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Nike-Hoop-Summit-International-Rosters-Announced-3145/ |date=December 4, 2020 }}. Draftexpress.com (March 23, 2009). Retrieved on 2011-06-14.</ref> and he was also selected to play in the 2009 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] where he scored a game-high 21 points and was named [[Most valuable player|MVP]] for the black team, while [[Renardo Sidney]] was named MVP for the white team.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4080678 Big men shine in Jordan Brand Classic]. Sports.espn.go.com. Retrieved on June 14, 2011.</ref>
He finished his senior season averaging 28.1 points, 13.3 rebounds, 5.0 blocks, 3.0 steals and 2.0 assists per game and holds the career records in points (2,341), rebounds (1,511) and blocked shots (741).<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|url=http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/favors_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Favors Player Bio|access-date=August 6, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100419135822/http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/favors_derrick00.html|archive-date=April 19, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Derrick Favors cropped.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Favors with Georgia Tech in 2010]]
Favors committed to [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]] in January 2009, which he chose over [[University of Georgia|Georgia]] and [[North Carolina State University|North Carolina State]].<ref>{{cite news|title=South Atlanta's Favors commits to Tech|work=The Gainesville Times|url=https://www.gainesvilletimes.com/sports/georgia-tech-yellow-jackets/south-atlantas-favors-commits-to-tech/|access-date=July 14, 2020}}</ref>

Favors played both power forward and center for [[Paul Hewitt]]'s Yellow Jackets. The frontcourt consisted of a three-man rotation of Favors, [[Gani Lawal]] and [[Zach Peacock]]. In ACC games, he averaged 11.8 points and 8.7 rebounds per game and shot 62.5% from the field. He also helped lead the Yellow Jackets to the [[ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] finals against [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. During the tournament, he posted 17 points, 9.8 rebounds and 3 blocks per game.

Favors was named ACC Rookie of the Year and to the ACC All-Freshman Team.<ref name="autogenerated1"/>

==Professional career==

===New Jersey Nets (2010–2011)===
On April 9, 2010, Favors announced he would forgo his final three years of college eligibility to enter the [[2010 NBA draft]]<ref>[http://www.slamonline.com/nba/derrick-favors-to-declare-for-nba-draft/ Derrick Favors to Declare for NBA Draft]</ref> where he was subsequently selected with the third overall pick by the [[New Jersey Nets]]. Favors was 19 years 104 days when he made his NBA debut, thus becoming the youngest player ever to set foot on court for the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Young Jarrett Allen impresses teammates in NBA debut|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/nets/young-jarrett-allen-impresses-teammates-in-nba-debut-t83848|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617043518/https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/nets/young-jarrett-allen-impresses-teammates-in-nba-debut-1.14570050|url-status=live|archive-date=June 17, 2018|website=newsday.com|access-date=February 27, 2018|date=October 21, 2017}}</ref> In just his third game with the Nets on October 31, 2010, against Miami, he recorded his first career double-double with 13 points and 13 rebounds (10 offensive) in a 101–78 loss.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20101103001326/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301031017 LeBron James leads balanced effort as Heat blow out Nets]</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2011–2019)===
On February 23, 2011, Favors was traded, along with [[Devin Harris]], two future first-round picks, and cash considerations to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Deron Williams]].<ref>{{cite web| title = Jazz Obtains Harris and Favors from New Jersey | url = https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/deron_williams_trade.html | date = February 23, 2011 | access-date = February 24, 2011 | work =NBA.com}}</ref> He went on to score a season-high 17 points on April 9 against San Antonio.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110413214132/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310409024 Richard Jefferson powers Spurs' reserves to win over Jazz]</ref>

On October 19, 2013, Favors signed a four-year contract extension with the Jazz.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14577 |title=Utah Jazz sign Derrick Favors to contract extension |access-date=October 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020120558/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14577 |archive-date=October 20, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On November 1, 2014, Favors scored a then career-high 32 points in a 118–91 win over the Phoenix Suns.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141101/PHXUTA/gameinfo.html |title=Favors powers Jazz to first win, 118–91 over Suns |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 2, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330124405/http://www.nba.com/games/20141101/PHXUTA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 30, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On November 12, 2015, he recorded 25 points, 12 rebounds and a career-high 7 blocks in a loss to the Miami Heat.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151112/UTAMIA/gameinfo.html |title=Bosh scores 25, Johnson adds 17 and Heat top Jazz 92–91 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 13, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151113051001/http://www.nba.com/games/20151112/UTAMIA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=November 13, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 5, 2015, he scored a career-high 35 points in a 122–119 overtime win over the Indiana Pacers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151205/INDUTA/gameinfo.html |title=Favors scores 35 as Jazz beat Pacers 122–119 in OT |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=December 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151220105115/http://www.nba.com/games/20151205/INDUTA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 20, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 25, 2016, Favors returned to the floor after a 16-game absence due to a back problem. He played 19 minutes off the bench and recorded 14 points and 5 rebounds in a loss to the Detroit Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160125/DETUTA/gameinfo.html |title=Jackson scores 29, Pistons defeat Jazz 95–92 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 26, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161017183700/http://www.nba.com/games/20160125/DETUTA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=October 17, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 13, 2018, in a 110–79 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]], Favors climbed to 10th place on Utah's all-time rebounding list with 3,602 rebounds. He passed former Utah center [[Mehmet Okur]], who pulled down 3,599 rebounds with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975759|title=Hot start propels Jazz to 110–79 win over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=March 13, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> On April 11, 2018, in a 102–93 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Favors played in his 500th game with the Jazz, becoming the 12th player in franchise history to reach the milestone.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975975|title=Blazers claim No. 3 seed with 102–93 win over Utah|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=April 12, 2018}}</ref> In Game 2 of the Jazz's first-round playoff series against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Favors had career playoff bests of 20 points and 16 rebounds in a 102–95 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401029440|title=Mitchell lifts Jazz past Thunder 102–95 to even series|work=ESPN.com|date=April 18, 2018|access-date=April 18, 2018}}</ref>

On July 6, 2018, Favors re-signed with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-agree-terms-favors-exum-and-neto|title=Jazz Agree to Terms with Favors, Exum and Neto|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}</ref> On January 11, 2019, he had a then season-high 13 rebounds in a 113–95 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], thus passing [[Greg Ostertag]] (3,978) for fourth place on the franchise's all-time rebounding list.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071303|title=Mitchell dominates, Jazz beat Lakers 113–95|work=ESPN.com|date=January 11, 2019|access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> On March 2, 2019, he had 23 points and tied a career best with 18 rebounds in a 115–111 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071616|title=Mitchell scores career-high 46 to lead Jazz past Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=March 2, 2019|access-date=March 3, 2019}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2019–2020)===
On July 7, 2019, Favors was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for two future second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans acquire Derrick Favors|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-derrick-favors|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019|date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> He made his Pelicans debut on October 22, recording six points, seven rebounds and two assists in a 130–122 overtime loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=VANVLEET SCORES CAREER-HIGH 34, RAPTORS TOP PELICANS 130-122 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900001 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 14, Favors grabbed a career-high twenty rebounds, alongside twenty points and three assists, in a 132–127 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. It was Favors' first game with twenty points and twenty rebounds in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HOLIDAY'S 36 POINTS PUSH PELICANS PAST CLIPPERS 132-127 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900164 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 18, 2020, he scored a season-high 22 points, alongside eleven rebounds and three assists, in a 133–130 loss to the Clippers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LEONARD, CLIPPERS RALLY TO BEAT PELICANS 133-130 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900626 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Return to Utah (2020–2021)===
On November 25, 2020, Favors signed a three-year, $27 million contract that reunited him with the [[Utah Jazz]] in free agency.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz sign Derrick Favors|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-derrick-favors|work=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2020|access-date=November 25, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jazz signing Jordan Clarkson ($52M) and Derrick Favors ($27M)|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/11/20/jazz-signing-jordan-clarkson-52m-and-derrick-favors-27m/|website=ProBasketballTalk {{!}} NBC Sports|date=November 21, 2020|access-date=November 21, 2020}}</ref> On December 23, he made his season debut for the Jazz, recording ten points, seven rebounds and three assists in a 120–100 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=GOBERT DOMINANT INSIDE, LILLARD STRUGGLES, JAZZ ROUT BLAZERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000020 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 1, 2021, Favors scored a season-high 14 points, alongside eleven rebounds and two assists, in a 106–100 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CONLEY SCORES 33 POINTS, JAZZ BEAT CLIPPERS 106-100 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000077 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 10, he grabbed a season-high 14 rebounds, alongside six points, in a 96–86 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=EARLY HOLE TOO BIG FOR PISTONS; JAZZ PREVAIL 96-86 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000141 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 8, Favors moved into tenth place on the Jazz's all-time scoring list, passing [[Mehmet Okur]] with 7,257 points.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Kyle|last1=Ireland|title=Jazz Center Derrick Favors Enters Top 10 On Franchise's All-Time Scoring List|url=https://kslsports.com/457140/jazz-center-derrick-favors-enters-top-10-on-franchises-all-time-scoring-list/|publisher=KSL.com|date=April 8, 2021|access-date=July 30, 2021}}</ref> During the first round of the playoffs, the Jazz faced the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. On May 23, Favors played in his first playoff game since 2019, recording twelve points, eleven rebounds and four blocks in a 112–109 Game 1 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=8TH-SEEDED MEMPHIS BEATS NO. 1-SEEDED JAZZ IN SERIES OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000141 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Jazz eventually won the series in five games, but were eliminated in a six-game series by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during the second round.

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2021–2022)===
On July 30, 2021, Favors was traded, alongside a future first-round pick, to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Derrick Favors and Future First-Round Draft Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-favors-210730|website=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=July 31, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Oklahoma City Thunder get future first-round NBA draft pick, Derrick Favors from Utah Jazz|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31919563/oklahoma-city-thunder-get-future-first-round-nba-draft-pick-derrick-favors-utah-jazz-sources|publisher=ESPN|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=July 30, 2021}}</ref> He made his Thunder debut on October 20, recording four points and nine rebounds in a 107–86 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Coon|title=JAZZ DOMINATE THUNDER, CLAIM 107-86 VICTORY|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100011|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2021|access-date=February 17, 2023}}</ref> On November 4, Favors grabbed a season-high twelve rebounds, alongside ten points, in a 107–104 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Beacham|title=THUNDER ROAR BACK TO BEAT LAKERS AGAIN, 107-104|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100123|website=NBA.com|date=November 5, 2021|access-date=February 17, 2023}}</ref> On February 11, 2022, he scored a season-high 16 points, alongside nine rebounds and three blocks, in a 100–87 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Gelston|title=EMBIID'S 25 POINTS, 19 BOARDS LIFT 76ERS PAST THUNDER 100-87|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100840|website=NBA.com|date=February 12, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}}</ref> On March 31, Favors was ruled out for the remainder of the season with lower back soreness.<ref>{{cite web|first=Clemente|last=Almanza|title=OKC Thunder news: Mark Daigneault provides injury updates on Kenrich Williams and Derrick Favors|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2022/03/31/okc-thunder-news-mark-daigneault-provides-injury-updates-on-kenrich-williams-and-derrick-favors/|work=USA Today|date=March 31, 2022|access-date=April 1, 2022}}</ref>

On September 30, 2022, Favors was traded, alongside [[Ty Jerome]], [[Maurice Harkless]], [[Théo Maledon]] and a future second-round pick, to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[David Nwaba]], [[Sterling Brown (basketball)|Sterling Brown]], [[Trey Burke]], and [[Marquese Chriss]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Hannah|last=Peery|title=Rockets Complete Trade with Oklahoma City|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-with-oklahoma-city|website=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2022|access-date=October 1, 2022}}</ref> On October 17, Favors was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Rockets Waive Derrick Favors|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/10/rockets-to-waive-derrick-favors.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 14, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}}</ref>

On January 11, 2023, Favors signed a 10-day contract with his hometown team the [[Atlanta Hawks]] but saw no playing time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign Veteran Center Derrick Favors to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-veteran-center-derrick-favors-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 11, 2023|access-date=January 11, 2023}}</ref>

===Windy City Bulls (2023–2024)===
On October 16, Favors signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|title=OFFICIAL: We have signed center Derrick Favors and forward Kahlil Whitney to camp contracts.|number=1714069165038879018|user=chicagobulls|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2023}}</ref> but was waived two days later.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|title=Roster Update: We have waived Derrick Favors and Kahlil Whitley.|number=1714657733255778518|user=chicagobulls|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 24, 2023}}</ref> On November 2, he joined the [[Windy City Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Windy City Bulls Announce 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/the-windy-city-bulls-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}}</ref>
